![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14058598/assets/9babf4c2ec631b3b872760261a46c3552cb93b93df90515ff0605c15043841ca.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}(x+y)\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the path along a circle of radius $4,$ traversed from the point $(-4,0)$ to the point $(4,0),$ as shown above?

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$*
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a part-circle of radius $4$ centered at $O.$ It can be parameterized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,\pi \le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=x+y,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\  & =4(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }4(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot (-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-16{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
